title: Domestic Violence Call
summary: On-scene steps for a domestic violence call, from arrival to the DV report.

steps.text: Stage and approach with backup; check call history and prior DV at the address
Separate the parties, out of sight and hearing of each other
Check for injuries and request EMS when needed
Ask about weapons in the home and on the parties
Body-worn camera on for the entire contact
Confirm a DV relationship
steps.detail: Current or former spouse or household member, child in common or expected, or dating relationship (2C:25-19)

steps.text: Identify the offense (predicate act) and whether probable cause exists
Interview each party and witnesses separately, including children if appropriate
Check the DV central registry for existing restraining orders
If both parties are injured, identify the primary aggressor
Run the mandatory arrest go-by
steps.detail: Injury, warrant, order violation or weapon = mandatory arrest

steps.text: Do not arrest a victim who used reasonable force in self-defense
Seize weapons that put the victim at risk of serious bodily injury
With any firearm, also seize the FPIC and handgun purchase permits
Inventory seized items in the DV report and forward per county prosecutor procedure
Give the victim written notice of rights, in a language they understand
Explain the TRO process and help with an application if requested
Photograph injuries and the scene
Provide the NJ DV hotline and local victim advocate information
If children were present or harmed, follow policy for notifying DCP&P
Complete the DV offense report for every DV incident, even with no arrest
Sign complaints as required; note bail or release conditions
Notify a supervisor per policy

note: Follow your department's policy and current AG directives. Not yet verified against official sources.
